variants.name: Interface-based passive view for Android
variants.idiom_name: View interface implemented by Activity/Fragment + plain presenter class (no Android imports)
variants.implementation_notes: The Android-era MVP shape: an interface declares the screen vocabulary, the Activity or Fragment implements it, and the presenter is a plain Kotlin class holding the interface plus the model - no Android imports, so JVM tests run with a fake view. Gestures call presenter methods directly; the presenter pushes every change back through the interface. Keep this form for existing view-system screens; for new code Android's official architecture guidance prefers state holders (ViewModel) with unidirectional data flow, which is why the supervising variant below exists for teams that keep MVP.
pitfalls: Storing an Activity/Fragment in the presenter leaks it across configuration changes; detach in onDestroy and re-attach to the recreated view, or keep the view reference nullable and clear it.
A presenter that outlives the screen must own no view reference at all; otherwise rotation silently keeps the destroyed Activity alive.
Android view calls must happen on the main thread; a presenter resumed from Dispatchers.IO has to hand results back with a main-dispatcher continuation.

variants.name: Supervising Controller with delegated observable properties
variants.idiom_name: view state as Delegates.observable properties (or StateFlow-like holders) + presenter for input and complex logic
variants.implementation_notes: Kotlin's delegated properties give the Supervising Controller variant a terse mechanism: screen fields are properties backed by Delegates.observable (or a small observable state holder), so assigning a value from the presenter notifies the view's binding code, while the presenter still owns input handling and the effects delegation cannot express. Interface delegation (`class Screen(...) : StationView by viewActions`) can forward the contract to a small wrapper when a screen implements several interfaces. Choose this when the screen is mostly field mapping and the team accepts some untested view behaviour; choose the interface variant when all display decisions must be testable.
pitfalls: Delegates.observable fires on the assigning thread; a presenter updating state from a background thread must hop to the main dispatcher before touching views.
The observable callback closes over the view, and the view may outlive or precede it; clear the callback when the screen is destroyed or route updates through a state holder owned per screen.
Mixing delegated observables with ViewModel/StateFlow in the same screen creates two sources of truth for the same field.
